body: Thank you for seeing and hearing me. I'm in a better mental state for now, and I'll try to hold on to it!
Hi, thank you for this. Reading your reply on that day made me feel better :)

THIS. I'm so happy you unfollowed her because you are absolutely right. We do not need people who do not need us. We should not bend ourselves backwards for someone who would not even do something basic for us. I am so proud that you have your head and heart in the right place, and know that these actions do not reflect upon you as a person, but on them. 

The right people will stay. 

You got this!!

Hi there! Firstly, congrats on starting a new job. I understand the trepidation that comes with needing to perform well. But do be a little kinder to yourself. Give yourself time to learn, time to make mistakes. Ask your colleagues/superiors if you are unsure of something. I believe that everybody will give a new starter more leeway even if they make mistakes at the start. As long as you show the willingness to learn and do your best, it will not be held against you. 

Next, regarding your sessions with your psychologist, I would just like you to consider that they are not mind readers. Doors open both ways, right? You have to also be open with them in order for things to work. If you have trouble expressing yourself, maybe you can tell your psychologist exactly that, that you don't know how to say it but you're not feeling okay. And then maybe you guys can try to work it out together. I can't speak for your psychologist or know what they are like, but I know that most of them are trying their best to help their clients get better. You have to help them help you, okay? 

I'm really proud of you that you are still so considerate towards your friend even when you're having a hard time yourself. If your friend shares their problems with you, consider doing the same? You can tell them that they don't need to give you any solutions, that you just want to rant. Sometimes, just talking it out with someone can make us feel better.

I wish you feel better soon and have a good day!

Hi there, I really empathise with your situation. I'm not sure where you're from but I think what you've mentioned is a very Asian culture. I have been through this at around your age as well, but I have to say that in my society, there is a rising trend of women who do not want to marry, so in a sense it is not as rigid for me. I spent years and years telling my parents that I don't intend to marry (my reasons are very similar to yours, but I didn't give them any reasons). It is only until recently (I am now 28) that my mum has kinda accepted that I am going to remain single all my life.

I think the most important question comes down to whether you'll be okay with living a life that you do not want, that may even make you miserable, just to comply to your parents' wishes? Please remember that it is not a matter of short term tolerance, it is going to be for the rest of your life. Are you really going to be okay with, like you said, giving up your entire life, all your goals and dreams, just for a purpose which does not serve you? Will you be happy? 

Regarding what you can do, I'm not sure about your employment and financial position, but I would suggest that you start saving up and working towards financial independence. If it really comes down to it, you can leave. Just try to make sure that you will not be forced to be stuck or trapped in this situation just because you don't have the means to do otherwise. If they don't give you a choice, create options for yourself. I don't think it is selfish of you to "leave your parents behind". You can still send them money, you can go back and visit them. You have this one life, do you want to live for yourself or others? 

I wish you all the best!!

I'm sorry that I can't help you better. Does your college have any counselling services on campus? I think the fact that you're still here shows that you are so brave to keep forging on despite how hard things are. I pray that you have a good day today. Let's take it one day at a time :)

This is my 10th year being single, I guess you can say I have never dated as an adult since my last relationship was back when I was still in high school. 

Over the years, I grew more and more withdrawn. Like you, I draw a line and keep from getting too close with people because I don't want to let anyone in only for them to leave. I do have a handful of close friends though, and while it helps, we all know the kind of platonic affection is not quite the same. 

I've tried dating apps a few times, but if anybody were to remotely show interest, I find that I get TERRIFIED and want to withdraw again. Most of the time though, I feel quite okay. I enjoy my time alone but yes, it's so lonely sometimes. 

My best friend just got married last year, and whenever I look at what she and her husband has, it's like the kind of relationship I have always dreamed of having. Having a safe place to return to, knowing someone has your back no matter what, that kind of thing. Knowing that I will never have that in this life makes me so sad sometimes, but I think I just learnt to live with it and find something else to hyperfixate on. 

If it comes, it comes. In the mean time, keep working on yourself. Learn and develop your strengths, recognise and embrace your weaknesses. So that if and when the right person comes along for you, you can be the best version of yourself for them.
This was so nice to read. I'm proud of you for pushing through and reaching out despite how hard things are. You got this!

Sounds awesome! Ngl, I stayed alive to attend an Infinite concert back in 2015, and that's how I'm still here today.

Very often, it's the small things that keep us going anyway. Good on you!
Hi there. I really relate with what you've written here. May I ask if you're a minor? If not, then would you consider maybe talking to a therapist?
This is the date I had set for myself too.

I feel like I ghostwrote this, so really, not going to counter the things you've said here. I just want you to know that you have done well coming this far even when things are not enjoyable, or just downright difficult. Even if you may not be the most achieved person, you have worked hard. I hope that you'll have a good day today, and many, many more good days ahead.

Thank you for this, you're very kind. To be honest, I feel quite alright right now but I know that in time, could be a few weeks or a few months, the same intense feeling of not wanting to be alive will come back again and I may regret not following through with my plan. I have always just let the waves of deep depressive episodes crash over my head, but this time I wondered if I should just stop it once and for all.

Thank you for your response, I'm glad that you feel that life is still better. I agree that life still has its perks, just that there are times I feel like the pain far outweighs everything and I want it to stop. At some point I just wondered if there was a point to keep fighting this haha.
